extracted.intended_audience: life-sciences researchers/authors, peer reviewers, journal editors, and publishers interested in preprint and peer-review innovations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for conducting and using peer review of life‑science manuscripts before journal submission (portable/reusable reviews intended for posting with preprints and transfer to affiliated journals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific rigor and merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts submitted to Review Commons will be judged exclusively for their scientific rigor and merit, without regard to any journal to which they might ultimately be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should focus on the intrinsic quality, validity, and merit of the science rather than on fit to a particular journal’s subjective criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers will be asked to evaluate the technical rigor of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should address experimental design, methodology, data quality, analysis, and whether conclusions are supported by evidence; reviewers should point out technical weaknesses that need correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionable suggestions for improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are expected to make suggestions for improvements to the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be constructive and actionable—identifying specific changes, additional experiments, analyses, or clarifications that would strengthen the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of potential value to specific communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should comment on the potential value of the work to specific research communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate relevance, interest, and likely impact for particular subfields or user communities, to help authors and editors understand audience fit and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review independence from journal fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews are conducted without regard to any particular journal’s standards for novelty, scope, or subjective editorial priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should not gatekeep based on perceived journal prestige or editorial scope; focus on whether the science is sound and valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency through public posting (TRiP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can direct Review Commons to post the reviews and their responses publicly to bioRxiv via the Transparent Review in Preprints (TRiP) project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public posting provides rich context for readers of the preprint and increases transparency of the review process; reviews and responses become part of the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portability and reusability of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons facilitates transfer of the manuscript, referee reports, and author responses to affiliated journals so reviews can be reused across submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can reuse peer review evaluation when submitting to other journals, reducing redundant re-review and accelerating publication timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal commitment to use referee reports with minimal additional input
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliated journals commit to use the Review Commons referee reports for their independent editorial decisions and to seek minimal additional expert input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may rely on existing referee comments to make efficient decisions; any additional reviewer input should be limited and targeted to remaining issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency and reduction of reviewer burden
rubrics_metrics.description: The platform is intended to reduce repeated re-review at multiple journals and thereby accelerate publishing and save reviewer time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By enabling a single rigorous review cycle prior to journal submission, the system aims to conserve community reviewing resources and shorten decision timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity of review
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons seeks to address objectivity in peer review as a core principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be impartial and focused on evidence and methodological soundness rather than subjective or non-scientific factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with existing publishing systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The service is designed to be compatible with existing journals' publishing systems and workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processes (posting, transfer of reviews, editorial use) should integrate with current journal submission and editorial decision workflows to enable uptake by publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and evaluation of service efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: During an initial evaluation period, partners will monitor the efficacy of the service and share results with the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance metrics, community feedback, and outcome tracking should be collected and analyzed to inform possible expansion and improvements.
